Sean —

Thanks again for the intro call today. As we discussed, Nimbus needs a concrete Mutual Action Plan tied to a short evaluation window so procurement can move to PO within 2–3 weeks. Key asks from our side:
- A focused perf benchmark that captures p50/p95 latency, time-to-first-token (TTFT), steady-state throughput, and concurrency behavior at realistic payloads.
- Regional samples: US (us-west), EU (eu-central), APAC (ap-southeast). We need both cold and warm KV-cache numbers and a failover run that simulates a region outage.
- A short rollout plan for the production cutover and any routing / multi-region failover recommendations.

Can you share a MAP doc with the perf test plan and proposed close timeline? Ideally we run probes on our side and share results by EOD Tuesday (14th).

From: sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com

Quentin — thanks, clear ask. Attaching a short MAP and an executable perf plan (MAP v3) that we can both sign off on. Highlights here:

1) Evaluation scope (5 business days):
   - Benchmarks: p50/p95 latency, TTFT, tokens/sec throughput, and per-request compute cost estimates.
   - Concurrency sweep: 1 / 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 concurrent connections using real prompt shapes (patient-summary and triage-chat).
   - Warm vs cold (3 warm runs after a warming window).

2) Regional tests:
   - US (us-west-2), EU (eu-central-1), APAC (ap-southeast-1).
   - Multi-region routing: baseline routing to local region, fallback policy to nearest-region; forced-failover run where primary region is taken out of rotation.

3) Success criteria (for go/no-go):
   - p95 latency under 200ms for US, under 300ms for EU, under 400ms for APAC for typical chat prompts at 1–2k tokens TTFT; envelope tolerances provided in the doc.
   - No more than 20% throughput regression on failover.

4) Close timeline:
   - 11 Jun: MAP v3 shared (this email).
   - 14 Jun: Nimbus to return probe CSV + notes.
   - 15 Jun: joint review; finalize SOW and PO routing.
   - 25 Jun: target production cutover (canary first 10% traffic).

Attachments: nimbus_MAP_v3.pdf (MAP with test matrix), regional_probe_template.csv (template).

Monica and Evelyn — can you please review the test matrix and add any infra-specific notes (kernel selection, quantization variant used, concurrency recommendations) and confirm availability next week to support the probe runs?

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher

From: monica.patel@redwood.inference.com

Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + perf expectations

Thanks — read the MAP and added test-level notes inline (see attached matrix). Quick summary from engineering for the evaluation plan:

Test harness: k6 with custom token loader to simulate TTL-sensitive KV-cache patterns. We will provide a small cluster of probes pre-warmed from Redwood hosted endpoints; Quentin can optionally run the same harness from Nimbus private infra to compare network delta.

Model/config used for baseline: open-llama-34b variant (quantized q4f16) — we recommend this variant for initial latency/throughput balance. If Nimbus wants lower-cost trajectory, we can run a second pass with int8 quantization (expected +10–20% latency, -30–40% cost).

Key metrics we will report back in the CSV:
- p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, TTFT_ms, tokens_per_sec, requests_per_sec, avg_gpu_util, kv_cache_hit_rate, error_rate

Probe matrix (per-region):
- Warm single-request baseline (1 client)
- Concurrency sweep (4, 8, 16, 32)  — each sweep 2 minutes steady state after warmup
- Burst test: 2x expected peak for 60s to verify autoscaling triggers and soft-failure behavior
- Failover run: remove primary region from routing for 3 minutes and measure tail impact across requests/sec and p95

Evelyn — tagging you for routing policy note: we recommend sticky KV-cache within region and 3s soft-redirect to fallback region; this keeps TTFT bounded for active sessions while allowing quick failover for new sessions. Also we suggest a canary routing window during production cutover (10% flows to new routing policy for 24h).

I'll stand up the test harness and share the commands + shortened AMI snapshot for Nimbus on Friday.

-Monica
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.inference.com

From: Quentin Price <quentin.price@nimbushealth.com>

Cc: monica.patel@redwood.inference.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 18:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: regional performance probe plan + close timeline

Team — we completed an initial probe pass (attached regional_probe_results_20260614.csv, routing_failover_trace_20260614.zip). Notes below (raw from our ops run):

Summary numbers (median of runs in CSV):
- US (us-west-2): p50 32ms, p95 78ms, TTFT 48ms, throughput (tokens/sec) 820, concurrency stable to 16 before latency climbs 25%
- EU (eu-central-1): p50 64ms, p95 115ms, TTFT 92ms, tokens/sec 720, p95 impacted by cross-region WAN; concurrency stable to 8
- APAC (ap-southeast-1): p50 120ms, p95 230ms, TTFT 200ms, tokens/sec 560, high variation during 32-concurrency run

Failover measurement (forced primary down for 3 minutes):
- Multi-region fallback to nearest-region added +45–90ms p95 tail depending on originating region. Aggregate throughput dropped ~18% under failover (consistent with your 20% threshold).

Other observations:
- KV-cache warm runs materially improved TTFT (avg TTFT reduced by ~35%) — sticky per-region routing helps here.
- Error spike (0.9%) observed during APAC 32-concurrency burst; logs show queueing on the request ingress.

Next asks:
1) Can Redwood run a short tuned pass with the recommended sticky routing and 3s soft-redirect to confirm TTFT behavior?
2) Please confirm canary plan and whether Redwood will provide an SLA appendix for the Dedicated pool we plan to purchase.

Quentin
Director of Platform Ops, Nimbus Health
quentin.price@nimbushealth.com
